title: Safeguarded per-request KV quantization controller for runtime cost/quality tradeoffs
creator: Priya Raman
description: Experiment and implement a runtime controller that chooses a KV cache storage format (FP8 / INT8 / INT4 / FP16 fallback) on a per-request basis. The controller uses lightweight signals (prompt length, cohort history of quality deltas, uncertainty proxy from next-token logits, route / model variant, and recent latency headroom) to select the most aggressive compression that preserves output quality within defined tolerances. Key goals: reduce GPU memory pressure and average token cost while avoiding customer-visible quality regressions and preventing oscillation in format selection across heatmap cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: Controller implemented as a pluggable runtime stage with feature flag gated rollout
Per-request decision latency < 250us added to request path (median)
End-to-end P95 latency increase < 5% on sampled production traffic when enabled
Quality regression (measured by n-gram BLEU / embedding cosine / prompt-specific evals) below configured threshold (default: 1.5% relative) for 99% of sampled cohorts
Automated fallback to FP16 for requests that exceed uncertainty threshold
Integration with Console dashboards (per-format QPS, memory savings, quality deltas) and rollout hooks (canary/A-B/kill switch)
implementation_notes: Decision inputs: prefix length bucket, token-zipf score, per-customer cohort recent quality delta, model variant compatibility map, remaining KV-memory budget for shard
Encoder: map candidate quant modes to expected memory reduction and median quality delta from offline sims; keep these profiles in a compact telemetry table
Safeguard: hysteresis window (default 30s) to prevent flip-flopping on borderline requests; implement short-term smoothing of cohort deltas
Fallback path: synchronous FP16 read for requests flagged as high-uncertainty and then async re-sync cached compact representation when quality stabilizes
Failure modes: plan for degraded throughput if fallback rate > 10%; add early-exit to disable controller when degraded
Telemetry: track per-request selected mode, reason code, estimated vs observed quality delta, latency delta, and whether fallback occurred
progress_updates: 2026-02-25: Kickoff — architecture sketched with runtime team. Agreed controller will be a thin policy module invoked after routing but before KV lookup. (Design doc draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/kv-per-request-quant-controller)

2026-02-28: Bench harness created to replay production-sampled traces (1M requests) and simulate quantized KV reads. Baseline: FP16 KV cache. Synthetic dataset: internal 'kb-chat-sampled-v2' with 10k evaluation prompts

2026-03-03: Microbench results: INT4 compaction reduces KV memory by ~62% and improves effective cache hit throughput by 18% in the simulator; median generation latency increased 6% and quality metric (embedding cosine to FP16) drops 2.4% on average for short-prefix chats

2026-03-05: FP8 mixed-mode (mantissa-first variant) shows best cost/quality tradeoff — ~38% memory reduction with <0.8% quality delta across eval set. Decided to prefer FP8/INT8 primary, INT4 only for clearly low-importance cohorts
2026-03-07: Implemented uncertainty proxy using normalized top2-logit gap and prefix entropy. Tuned threshold to keep fallback rate to FP16 at 3% in synthetic traffic
2026-03-09: PR opened for controller core + feature flag and tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287. Request review from @ana-sec and @xueng

2026-03-10: Canary plan approved: 1% of production traffic (low-latency, non-SLA customers) for 48h with continuous monitors for quality regressions and fallback spikes. Dashboard prototype: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/kv-quant/controller-canary
